prompt: How does a catalyst increase the rate of a reaction?
options: It increases the kinetic energy of the particles
It provides an alternative pathway with a lower activation energy
It shifts the position of equilibrium to the right
It increases the enthalpy change of the reaction
explanation: A catalyst offers an alternative reaction pathway with lower $E_a$, so a greater proportion of collisions have $E \geq E_a$. It does not change $\Delta H$ or the equilibrium position.
